question: Will South African police officially state that the Ekurhuleni women's killings are the work of a single serial killer before October 3, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is explicit, repeated official denial: SAPS spokespeople, the acting Gauteng commissioner, the deputy national commissioner (21 Sept briefing) and the acting police minister all said within the last 8 days that no serial-killer conclusion has been reached and that multiple/separate perpetrators remain live. The question's fine print excludes exactly the language SAPS is using ('not discounting the possibility', 'investigating whether'). Recent evidence moves away from YES: the 9th case (Jabulile Ntimba) is being prosecuted as a relationship/love-triangle killing, with one of three arrestees already released for lack of evidence, and the July 15 arrestee is still linked to only one death. Bodies span ~25-35 km, and no forensic/DNA turnaround date has been announced - SA's forensic backlog makes a linkage announcement in 11 days unlikely even on a presidential-priority case. Residual YES paths: DNA from the clustered Kempton Park/Rhodesfield bodies returning fast enough for SAPS to announce same-perpetrator linkage across 3+ cases, or a new arrest with immediate multi-case attribution, under heavy political/protest pressure. Thin, one-sided evidence keeps me near the base rate.
calls.reference_class: Police agencies in high-profile serial-murder scares that have publicly and repeatedly declined to confirm a single perpetrator, reversing to an affirmative official single-perpetrator/linkage statement within an arbitrary ~11-day window
